title: Reject duplicate JSON members
invariant: An exact duplicate member in a security-bearing JSON object must be rejected rather than resolved by last-write-wins parsing.

title: Require exact JSON member spelling
invariant: Case-folded aliases must not satisfy an exact security vocabulary or coexist as a decoy beside the exact member.

title: Reject trailing JSON documents
invariant: A parser must consume exactly one complete security-bearing JSON value plus optional whitespace.

title: Confirm removal only from a coherent response envelope
invariant: A serializer-rendered payload must not establish a removal that the invocation classification or the independently recorded fault state contradicts, and an unmodelled classification establishes nothing.
limitations: single-envelope evidence only; no follow-up read is modelled
binary outcome: the case measures fact sufficiency, not an authority transition

title: Withhold a finding when no attributable analysis exists
invariant: A field read out of a record that does not exist, or that is not attributable to its stated producer, yields an undetermined finding rather than either a positive or a negative conclusion.
limitations: signature verification is modelled as a supplied boolean, not performed
three-valued fact output; this case is an input to an authority decision, not the decision itself

title: Require an attestation issued for the scope actually being gated
invariant: A verifiable signature establishes that a statement was issued, not that it was issued about the scope and subject the caller needs; validity is not relevance.
limitations: signature verification is modelled as a supplied boolean, not performed
scope matching is literal string equality; real scope algebras may be hierarchical

title: Establish containment only from an attributable measurement
invariant: A field the requesting party controls cannot establish a measured property of the boundary it sits behind, nor rebut an attributable measurement of it.
limitations: signature verification is modelled as a supplied boolean, not performed
probe freshness is out of scope for this case; see PF-012 for evidence anchoring

title: Confirm an irreversible retirement only from two coherent subsystems
invariant: An irreversible step requires each independent subsystem to have positively reported what the step assumes; a zero-valued field from a subsystem that produced no record is not a measurement of zero.
limitations: the inventory scan is modelled as complete; enumeration completeness is exercised separately in PF-011
binary outcome: this case measures fact sufficiency, not an authority transition

title: Fail when a required security test disappears
invariant: A previously required security test must not silently disappear from the discovered test universe.

title: Establish execution only from independently observed events
invariant: A report a process writes about itself cannot establish that the process did what it reports; only an independent observer's record of the events can, and it must cover every required name.
limitations: the supervisor's event stream is modelled as trustworthy input; stream integrity itself is out of scope
binary outcome: this case measures fact sufficiency, not an authority transition

title: Decide cleanup authority under an incomplete enumeration
invariant: One bounded page of a paginated enumeration establishes what it names, not what the rest of the enumeration would name; an irreversible authority transition requires evidence that the enumeration is complete.
limitations: GRANT is not reachable in this case: every workspace already holds a cleanup role
pagination is modelled as a single page plus a cursor, not as a full enumeration loop
listing consistency and concurrent writers are out of scope

title: Decide a grant when the only attestation is anchored elsewhere
invariant: Cryptographic attributability establishes who produced an observation, not what the observation is about; an observation anchored to another subject or another generation supports neither a positive nor a negative authority transition for this one.
limitations: GRANT is not reachable in this case: every subject already holds a grant
signature verification is modelled as a supplied boolean, not performed
generation ordering is modelled as integer equality; real anchoring may use digests or epochs

title: Decide a trust-store entry when two modalities disagree
invariant: A service's account of what it did does not override an independent reading of what is actually stored; where the two accounts conflict, or where neither is available, no final authority transition is warranted.
limitations: signature verification is modelled as a supplied boolean, not performed
the readback is modelled as contemporaneous with the request; read-after-write timing is out of scope
a single readback is modelled, not quorum or repeated reads
